key_insight: In disordered lead-halide perovskite nanocrystal solids, exciton transport is controlled more by energetic disorder than by structural size/shape disorder.
engineering_relevance: Ligand length engineering can tune nanocrystal disorder and therefore guide the design of more efficient optoelectronic materials for LEDs, lasers, and solar cells.
method: Resolved exciton dynamics in space, time, and energy
Compared disorder effects across nanocrystal solids synthesized with different alkylamine ligand lengths
Linked transport behavior to structural polydispersity and quantum-confinement-driven energetic disorder
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that shorter ligands produce more polydisperse particles, while longer ligands yield more monodisperse but more energetically disordered nanocrystals, and the latter show less efficient exciton transport.
watch_item: Improving monodispersity alone may not enhance transport if ligand-induced quantum confinement increases energetic disorder.
paper_title: Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
